items.text: Among inpatient wards in a three-hospital network, does a tiered drug interaction alert display, compared with the standard display, increase the proportion of high-severity alerts with an appropriate prescriber response over six months, without increasing harm from suppressed moderate interactions?
items.population: Inpatient wards (clusters) and the high-severity interaction alerts raised on them
items.intervention: Tiered alert display set per ward
items.comparator: Standard display with every interaction interruptive
items.outcome: Proportion of high-severity alerts accepted or overridden appropriately, judged by pharmacists on a random sample

finer: Feasible within the vendor contract and the medication safety team's time if review is sampled; interesting to prescribers and the director; novel for this network; ethical with harm surveillance; relevant before the order set change.
summary: One PICOT question with a harm safeguard.
